bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 100-byte witness makes `tests/internal/fuzzers/parser_fuzzer.c` choose the JSON parser, allocate a non-NULL 15-byte `time_fmt`, leave `time_key` absent so `flb_parser_json_do()` later defaults it to `"time"`, set `time_keep = MK_FALSE`, and install one `Decode_Field` decoder rule for key `AAA` with JSON backend and `do_next` action before passing the remaining 75 bytes into `flb_parser_do()`. In the exact staged vulnerable checkout `7bc64f4d6f2f14ad4db7cf0d50683ad9abd6f3e0`, `flb_parser_json_do()` packs that trailing payload into heap buffer `mp_buf`, unpacks it as `map`, and aliases `tmp_out_buf = mp_buf`. Because `parser->decoders` is non-NULL, it then calls `flb_parser_decoder_do()`, but the saved ASan trace's first free is still at line 144 rather than the earlier line 113 `flb_free(mp_buf)`, so the only staged decoder outcome compatible with this witness is the helper's early no-match return: its initial key scan leaves `matched == -1`, returns `-1`, and never installs a replacement output buffer. The caller therefore skips the `ret == 0` re-unpack block, keeps `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf`, and reaches the later cleanup with the original unpacked `map` still active. Because `parser->time_fmt` is non-NULL, the function stays on the time-resolution path, derives `slen = 4` from the default `time_key = "time"`, and the reproduced crash at lines 144-145 proves the key scan reaches the `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` cleanup branch. That vulnerable cleanup first frees `mp_buf` at line 144 and then immediately frees `tmp_out_buf` at line 145 even though both names still alias the same 8192-byte allocation. AddressSanitizer therefore reports the second free at line 145, the previous free at line 144, and the allocation on the earlier `flb_pack_json_recs()` call path. The fixing commit makes this cleanup alias-aware: it frees once when `mp_buf == tmp_out_buf` and only frees both pointers when they differ. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, so the GT records the patch semantics without treating resolution as dynamically witnessed.

source.description: First non-harness project parser step that consumes the trailing witness payload and materializes the heap msgpack buffer later freed twice.
source.value_from: The exact staged 100-byte witness is split by `tests/internal/fuzzers/parser_fuzzer.c` into 25 configuration bytes and 75 parser-payload bytes. Static replay of the harness shows byte 0 selects `format = "json"`; byte 1 enables a non-NULL 15-byte `time_fmt`; bytes 17-20 leave `time_key` and `time_offset` NULL and set `time_keep = MK_FALSE`; byte 21 allocates one decoder list; bytes 22-24 configure its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`; the remaining bytes 25-99 beginning `7b 20 22 22 ... 7d 20 20` are passed here as `in_buf`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness turns the exact 100-byte witness into crash-relevant parser state and the trailing payload handed to project code. Byte 0 (`0x20`) makes `GET_MOD_EQ(4,0)` true, so format is JSON. Byte 1 (`0xff`) makes `time_fmt` non-NULL. Bytes 17-20 (`0x20 0x20 0x20 0x20`) leave `time_key` and `time_offset` NULL and set `time_keep = MK_FALSE`. Byte 21 (`0xff`) allocates a decoder list, and bytes 22-24 (`0x20 0x20 0x20`) configure its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. The remaining bytes 25-99 become the parser payload.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The NULL-key cleanup path starts by freeing `mp_buf` even though step 6 has left `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf` and the very next statement will free that alias again. The fix makes this cleanup alias-aware so the alias case is freed only once.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. After line 144 already freed the aliased allocation, this second free through `tmp_out_buf` hits the same 8192-byte region and triggers the reported double-free.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free` at `src/flb_parser_json.c:145`, with the previous free at line 144 and the original allocation originating from `flb_pack_json_recs()` on this call path.

parser_admitted.description: The witness's first control byte makes the harness create a JSON parser, so `flb_parser_do()` dispatches into `flb_parser_json_do()` instead of the regex, LTSV, or logfmt handlers.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 100-byte witness configures a JSON parser with non-NULL `time_fmt`, no explicit `time_key`, `time_keep = MK_FALSE`, and one `AAA` JSON decoder rule, then passes the remaining 75 bytes to `flb_parser_do()`.
Because the configured parser type is JSON, `flb_parser_do()` dispatches the trailing witness payload into `flb_parser_json_do()`.

The trailing payload is packed into `mp_buf`, unpacked as a map, and aliased into `tmp_out_buf`. The decoder helper's initial key scan finds no decoder match for the sole configured key `AAA`, returns `-1`, and leaves the alias intact, so time-resolution continues with default `time_key = "time"` until the key scan reaches the `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` cleanup branch.
The NULL-key cleanup frees `mp_buf` and then frees `tmp_out_buf` even though both names still refer to the same allocation, producing the saved ASan double-free at line 145.

fine_trace.note: Static replay of the exact 100-byte witness shows the harness has already consumed bytes 0-24 as parser configuration before this call: byte 0 (`0x20`) selects JSON; bytes 1-15 create a non-NULL 15-byte `time_fmt`; bytes 17-20 leave `time_key` and `time_offset` NULL and set `time_keep = MK_FALSE`; byte 21 (`0xff`) allocates a decoder list; bytes 22-24 (`0x20 0x20 0x20`) configure its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. The remaining 75 bytes are then passed here as the parser payload.

Source. `flb_parser_json_do()` consumes the trailing 75-byte payload from step 1 and materializes heap buffer `mp_buf`. The saved allocation stack shows the later double-freed 8192-byte region originates on this call path through `pack_json_to_msgpack()` and `tokens_to_msgpack()`.

The packed payload is accepted as a single record and successfully unpacked as a msgpack map; otherwise the function would have returned before the vulnerable cleanup path. This `map` object is the one later scanned for the time key on the crashing run.
Before any decoder result is considered, the outgoing buffer aliases the original packed buffer exactly: `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf` and `tmp_out_size == mp_size`.

Because step 1 configured a decoder list whose sole key is `AAA`, `flb_parser_json_do()` calls `flb_parser_decoder_do()`. In the helper's initial key scan, no map entry satisfies that decoder match, so `matched` remains `-1` and lines 286-289 return `-1` before any replacement output buffer is created or `*out_buf` is written. The later ASan free sites are consistent only with this early-return outcome, since any successful decoder rewrite would force the earlier line 113 free.

fine_trace.var: ret, out_buf, out_size, mp_buf, tmp_out_buf, map
fine_trace.note: Step 5 returns `-1`, so the caller does not enter the `ret == 0` re-unpack block. `tmp_out_buf` therefore stays aliased to `mp_buf`, `map` remains the original unpack result from step 3, and the later export block sees `mp_buf == tmp_out_buf`. The line 112 guard is false, so no free or nulling happens here and both names still reference the same live allocation.

The early return is not taken. Step 1 made `parser->time_fmt` non-NULL, so execution stays on the time-resolution path and reaches the later key scan instead of returning immediately after exporting `out_buf`.

Because the witness did not supply `time_key`, the false branch selects the default literal `"time"`, and `strlen(time_key)` computes `slen = 4`. That size is the filter used in the subsequent map-key scan.

While scanning the original unpacked `map`, the crashing iteration reaches a key slot whose `k->via.str.size` matches `slen = 4`, so the size filter does not continue. The saved crash at lines 144-145 proves the next guard sees `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` on this witness. Stage 01 artifacts do not dump the exact malformed key entry, so this step records only the observed branch condition needed for the cleanup path.

Root cause. Entering the NULL-key cleanup at step 9, the function frees `mp_buf` first even though step 6 left `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf`. That first free invalidates the only heap allocation through both aliases. The fix makes this alias case free only once.

Sink. Immediately after step 10, the cleanup frees `tmp_out_buf`, which still aliases the same address that line 144 just released. AddressSanitizer reports this second free at line 145 on `0x625000002900`, with the previous free at line 144.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_34116 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the exact staged `poc` to `flb-it-fuzz-parser_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ`. The harness consumed bytes 0-24 as parser configuration and bytes 25-99 as the parser payload, reproducing `AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free` at `flb_parser_json_do:145`.

format.contract: Exactly the staged 100-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_34116/poc`, consumed by `tests/internal/fuzzers/parser_fuzzer.c`. Byte 0 is `0x20`, so `data[0] % 4 == 0` and the harness selects the JSON parser. Byte 1 is `0xff`, so the harness allocates a non-NULL 15-byte `time_fmt`. Bytes 17-20 are `0x20 0x20 0x20 0x20`, so `time_key` and `time_offset` stay NULL and `time_keep = MK_FALSE`. Byte 21 is `0xff`, so a decoder list is created, and bytes 22-24 are `0x20 0x20 0x20`, configuring its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. The remaining bytes 25-99 are the exact 75-byte parser payload `7b 20 22 22 20 20 22 22 3a 34 2d 6c 70 73 76 41 41 3a 3a 45 45 45 51 5a 20 20 20 20 20 3a 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 22 22 20 20 20 20 20 22 22 20 20 20 20 20 22 22 20 20 22 22 20 20 20 20 20 7d 20 20`. On the witnessed run, `flb_parser_json_do()` packs that payload into `mp_buf`, `flb_parser_decoder_do()` finds no decoder match for the sole configured key `AAA` and returns `-1`, the caller therefore keeps `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf`, and the later `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` cleanup frees that aliased allocation twice at lines 144 and 145.
